presentation.sampleOutput:
# User Research Synthesis — Workspace onboarding interviews, September 2026

_Internal research report · 7 participants · 7 interviews · Sep 14, 2026 – Sep 22, 2026 · synthesised Oct 2, 2026 · participants are pseudonymous (P1…); redaction is pattern-based, so read it before sharing._

**At a glance** — 3 research questions; 5 findings supported by 2+ participants (1 high, 3 medium, 1 low confidence); top opportunity by evidence: O2 (5 participants): Let admins invite the colleague who holds the credentials to connect the first data source. 2 items kept separate as single-participant signals.

## Research questions

- **RQ1** How do new admins get their first workflow live, and where do they stall? — 2 findings
- **RQ2** What do admins expect from the first-week setup checklist? — 3 findings
- **RQ3** Who else gets involved before a workspace is rolled out to the team? — 0 findings

## Findings by research question

_Confidence counts distinct participants, never mentions. Answers to leading questions are weaker and do not count towards medium or high. See Method for the thresholds._

### RQ1 — How do new admins get their first workflow live, and where do they stall?

#### F1. New admins stall at connecting the first data source, before they build any workflow. — High confidence

Support: 5 of 7 participants (P1, P2, P3, P4, P5) · 1 only via leading questions (P3) · Contradict: 1 (P7) · Said: P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 · Did (observed): none

By segment (supporting/participants): Self-serve admins 3/4 (1 contradict) · Sales-assisted teams 2/3

_Note: stated only; no observed behaviour._

- “I got stuck on the very first screen, connecting our shipment database.” — P1, Sep 14 · [M1](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-01)
- “Connecting the patient-booking system. The API key lives with our IT contractor, so everything stopped there.” — P2, Sep 15 · [M2](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-02)
- “The first week was mostly waiting on credentials for the scheduling system.” — P5, Sep 18 · [M5](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-05)
- Contradicting: Note excerpt (notes, not verbatim speech): _She connected the print-queue database herself in about ten minutes using the setup guide._ — P7, Sep 22 · [M7](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-07)
- Quotes withheld (no quote consent): P4; their evidence still counts. Sources: [M4](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-04)

#### F2. Admins skip the template gallery and build their first workflow from a blank canvas. — Medium confidence

Support: 3 of 7 participants (P2, P5, P7) · Contradict: 0 · Said: P7 · Did (observed): P2, P5

By segment (supporting/participants): Self-serve admins 2/4 · Sales-assisted teams 1/3

- Observed (notes, not verbatim speech): _He opened the template gallery, closed it after a few seconds, and built the workflow from a blank canvas._ — P2, Sep 15 · [M2](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-02)
- Observed (notes, not verbatim speech): _She skipped the template gallery and started from a blank canvas._ — P5, Sep 18 · [M5](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-05)
- Note excerpt (notes, not verbatim speech): _She did not open the template gallery and started from a blank canvas._ — P7, Sep 22 · [M7](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-07)

### RQ2 — What do admins expect from the first-week setup checklist?

#### F3. Admins want the setup checklist to show what their teammates still have to do. — Medium confidence

Support: 3 of 7 participants (P3, P5, P6) · Contradict: 0 · Said: P3, P5, P6 · Did (observed): none

By segment (supporting/participants): Self-serve admins 0/4 · Sales-assisted teams 3/3

_Note: stated only; no observed behaviour._

- “I need the checklist to show me what my team still has to do, not just my own steps.” — P3, Sep 16 · [M3](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-03)
- “I want the checklist to list single sign-on and who on my team hasn't logged in yet.” — P5, Sep 18 · [M5](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-05)
- Quotes withheld (no quote consent): P6; their evidence still counts. Sources: [M6](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-06)

#### F6. Admins expect single sign-on to be a step in the setup checklist. — Medium confidence

Support: 3 of 7 participants (P3, P5, P6) · Contradict: 1 (P2) · Said: P3, P5, P6 · Did (observed): none

By segment (supporting/participants): Self-serve admins 0/4 (1 contradict) · Sales-assisted teams 3/3

_Note: stated only; no observed behaviour._

- “And single sign-on has to be on it, our security review asks for it first.” — P3, Sep 16 · [M3](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-03)
- “I want the checklist to list single sign-on and who on my team hasn't logged in yet.” — P5, Sep 18 · [M5](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-05)
- Contradicting: “We don't need single sign-on. We're eleven people.” — P2, Sep 15 · [M2](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-02)
- Quotes withheld (no quote consent): P6; their evidence still counts. Sources: [M6](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-06)

#### F4. A progress bar would motivate admins to finish the setup checklist. — Low confidence

Support: 2 of 7 participants (P1, P4) · 2 only via leading questions (P1, P4) · Contradict: 1 (P5) · Said: P1, P4 · Did (observed): none

By segment (supporting/participants): Self-serve admins 2/4 · Sales-assisted teams 0/3 (1 contradict)

_Note: rests only on answers to leading questions; stated only; no observed behaviour._

- “Yeah, I guess a progress bar would be nice.” — P1, Sep 14 · [M1](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-01) — ⚠ answer to a leading question (“Wouldn't a progress bar make you more likely to finish the checklist?”), flagged by pattern; weaker evidence
- Contradicting: “I ignore progress bars, to be honest.” — P5, Sep 18 · [M5](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-05)
- Quotes withheld (no quote consent): P4; their evidence still counts. Sources: [M4](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-04)

### RQ3 — Who else gets involved before a workspace is rolled out to the team?

No finding for this question is supported by 2 or more participants.

## Jobs, pains, workarounds and desired outcomes

### Jobs to be done

- **F7** Get recurring team hand-offs running on their own, without chasing people or filing IT tickets. — High confidence · 4 participants (P1, P2, P4, P7)
  - “I want the Monday hand-offs between dispatch and billing to run without me chasing people, and without filing an IT ticket every time.” — P1, Sep 14 · [M1](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-01)

### Pains

- **F8** The credentials for the first data source are held by someone else in the company. — Medium confidence · 3 participants (P1, P3, P5)
  - “I asked \[name\] in finance for the login and waited two days.” — P1, Sep 14 · [M1](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-01)

### Current workarounds

- **F9** Keep the hand-off in a shared spreadsheet until the workflow has earned trust. — Medium confidence · 3 participants (P2, P4, P6)
  - “We still run the reminders from a shared spreadsheet. Until I trust the workflow, the spreadsheet stays.” — P2, Sep 15 · [M2](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-02)

### Desired outcomes

- **F10** See one workflow run end to end on day one. — Low confidence · 2 participants (P1, P5)
  - “Seeing one workflow run end to end on day one. Then I'd trust it.” — P1, Sep 14 · [M1](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-01)

## Single-participant signals (not patterns)

- **F5** (finding, RQ3) Finance approves the plan before a sales-assisted workspace is rolled out. — P3 only
  - “Finance had to approve the plan before we could invite anyone.” — P3, Sep 16 · [M3](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-03)
- **F11** (pain) The pricing page does not say which plan includes audit logs. — P6 only

## Differences by segment

_Share of each segment's participants supporting the finding. Listed when the gap is 50+ percentage points; segments with fewer than 2 participants are left out._

| Finding | Self-serve admins (n=4) | Sales-assisted teams (n=3) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F7 Get recurring team hand-offs running on their own, without chasing people or filing IT tickets. | 4/4 | 0/3 |
| F3 Admins want the setup checklist to show what their teammates still have to do. | 0/4 | 3/3 |
| F6 Admins expect single sign-on to be a step in the setup checklist. | 0/4 | 3/3 |
| F4 A progress bar would motivate admins to finish the setup checklist. | 2/4 | 0/3 |

## Surprises

- **F2** Admins skip the template gallery and build their first workflow from a blank canvas. — medium confidence, 3 participants. We assumed: Templates are the main way new admins get started.

## Opportunities, ranked by evidence

_Ranked by distinct participants supporting the linked findings (not counting answers to leading questions), then all supporters, then fewest contradicting, then the strongest linked confidence. Not ranked by anyone's opinion of value or effort._

| # | Opportunity | Based on | Support | Contradict | Best confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | O2 Let admins invite the colleague who holds the credentials to connect the first data source. | F1, F8 | 5 (P1, P2, P3, P4, P5) | 1 (P7) | High confidence |
| 2 | O3 Make single sign-on and teammates' open tasks part of the sales-assisted checklist. | F3, F6 | 3 (P3, P5, P6) | 1 (P2) | Medium confidence |
| 3 | O4 Show a 'first workflow ran' moment on day one. | F10 | 2 (P1, P5) | 0 | Low confidence |
| 4 | O1 Add a progress bar to the setup checklist. | F4 | 2 (P1, P4), 2 only via leading questions | 1 (P5) | Low confidence |
| 5 | O5 Say on the pricing page which plan includes audit logs. | F11 | 1 (P6), not a pattern | 0 | Single participant |

## What we still don't know

- RQ3\: no finding is supported by 2 or more participants yet.
- F4 rests only on answers to leading questions; ask neutrally before relying on it.
- 1 session had no readable transcript; evidence from it comes from notes, which paraphrase.
- RQ3\: Whether IT or security reviews the workspace before rollout; only one participant described an approval step.

## Participants

| ID | Segment | Interview date | Evidence from | Consent | Evidence items |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Self-serve admins | Sep 14, 2026 [M1](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-01) | transcript | quotes OK | 5 |
| P2 | Self-serve admins | Sep 15, 2026 [M2](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-02) | transcript | quotes OK | 5 |
| P3 | Sales-assisted teams | Sep 16, 2026 [M3](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-03) | transcript | quotes OK | 5 |
| P4 | Self-serve admins | Sep 17, 2026 [M4](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-04) | transcript | no quotes | 4 |
| P5 | Sales-assisted teams | Sep 18, 2026 [M5](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-05) | transcript | quotes OK | 5 |
| P6 | Sales-assisted teams | Sep 21, 2026 [M6](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-06) | transcript | unknown, so no quotes | 3 |
| P7 | Self-serve admins | Sep 22, 2026 [M7](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-urs-07) | notes (transcript denied) | quotes OK | 3 |

1 participant excluded because consent was declined (not listed; 1 evidence item dropped).

## Method and coverage

- **Interviews**: 7 included; 2 listed but excluded (all participants declined consent; internal debrief, not an interview).
- **Transcripts**: 6 read, 1 denied, 0 unavailable, 0 not requested.
- **Evidence**: 30 items (25 from transcripts, 5 from notes; 2 observed behaviour). 3 answers to leading questions (1 flagged by the question-wording pattern); 5 without the question's wording. 7 quotes withheld for consent; 0 not checked against source text because the text was not in the bundle.
- **Confidence** (distinct participants; answers to leading questions only count towards low): High = 4+ supporting and at least 50% of the 7 participants, with contradicting participants at most 25% of supporting; Medium = 3+; Low = 2+ in total; Contested = at least as many contradict as support; Single = fewer than 2, never shown as a pattern.
- **Anonymity**: participants appear as P1, P2… and sessions as M1, M2…; names, organisations and emails listed privately in the bundle (and the parts of listed full names) are replaced with [name] or [organisation], and email addresses, phone numbers and web addresses with a placeholder, in every displayed field. This is pattern-based and can miss unlisted names, nicknames, misspellings, look-alike letters and unusual formats; it can also blank ordinary words that match a listed name. Meeting links open the original notes, which are not anonymised.
- **Sources**: Meeting list: Granola, ok (folder: Onboarding interviews); Transcripts: Granola, partial.
- **Gaps**: transcripts partial (1 transcript denied by workspace policy).

_Internal research document. The agent extracted and coded the evidence; the script validated citations and quotes, counted participants, computed confidence and pseudonymised the text._

listings.name: win-loss-analysis
listings.description: Build a win/loss report for the deals closed won and closed lost in a period. It takes the deal list from your CRM or a CSV export, reads every Granola call with each deal's account, and reports the top reasons you win and lose (counted by distinct deals, optionally amount-weighted) with customer quotes (whole sentences, checked against the call text when it is included) and meeting links, our head-to-head win rate against each competitor, stage-of-loss and segment cuts, objections raised before losses, no-decision losses kept apart from competitive ones, small-sample warnings, and deals with no call coverage. Use when someone asks "why did we lose deals last quarter?", "win/loss review for Q3", "what's beating us against <competitor>?" or "why are we winning?". On request only; it never writes to the CRM, and the Slack summary is a draft until someone approves it.

presentation.title: Win/Loss Analysis
presentation.summary: Analyzes won and lost deals using customer-call evidence and deal outcomes. Groups reasons and competitor comparisons by deal, highlights conflicting evidence, and avoids percentages on small samples.
benefits: Ranks win and loss reasons by how many different deals cite them (optionally weighted by deal amount), so one talkative account can't look like a trend.
Sources reasons to quotes, labelled AI notes or CRM fields. Whole-sentence quote checks do not verify context. Missing reasons stay “no recorded reason”.
Separates competitive losses from no-decision losses, showing deal-level head-to-head records and customer evidence about each competitor.
Cuts losses by stage and segment, lists objections raised before losses, and shows counts instead of percentages when a group has fewer than 5 deals.
Lists closed deals with no call coverage as gaps, works from your CRM or a CSV export, and never writes to the CRM; the Slack summary is a draft until you approve it.

# Win/Loss Analysis — Q3 2026

Jul 1 – Sep 30, 2026 · closed deals, as of Oct 5, 2026

**At a glance** — 12 closed deals: 5 won, 7 lost (win rate 42%). Losses: 3 competitive, 2 no decision, 1 other, 1 no recorded reason. Top loss reason: Price or value not justified (2 lost deals). Top win reason: Fast time to value (2 won deals). Most-seen competitor: Countwhistle, in 5 deals; we won 3 of 5 (60%). 2 deals have no call coverage.

_Counted by distinct deals: a deal with three calls that all mention price counts once. Percentages appear only when the group has at least 5 deals; smaller groups show counts. Every reason cites a customer quote from a call transcript, a labelled note excerpt, or a CRM field._

## Why we lose

### Competitive losses (3 deals)

_Lost to a named competitor, as recorded in a CRM field or in a cited loss reason._

1. **Price or value not justified** — 2 of 3 competitive losses
   - **Marrowby & Vane** (D-1002 · \$60,000 · lost at Proposal · we lost to Countwhistle): “But at sixty thousand against their forty, finance would not sign it.” — Procurement lead · [Marrowby & Vane decision call, Sep 10](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w04)
   - **Sallowfen Dental** (D-1010 · \$22,000 · lost at Proposal · we lost to Countwhistle): Note excerpt (AI meeting notes, not verbatim speech): _Chose Countwhistle; their quote came in roughly 30% lower for the same seats._ · [Sallowfen Dental decision, Sep 8](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w12b)
   - **Marrowby & Vane** (D-1002 · \$60,000 · lost at Proposal · we lost to Countwhistle): [CRM field “Closed lost reason”](https://crm.tamsquill.example/deals/D-1002): “Price”
   - Deals: Marrowby & Vane \(D-1002\); Sallowfen Dental \(D-1010\)
2. **Competitor was a better fit** — 1 of 3 competitive losses
   - **Wrenholt Clinics** (D-1007 · \$45,000 · lost at Negotiation · we lost to Pindleworth): “Pindleworth already runs our scheduling, so adding their module was the easy path.” — Clinical ops lead · [Wrenholt Clinics loss debrief, Sep 30](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w11)
   - Deals: Wrenholt Clinics \(D-1007\)
3. **Missing feature or capability** — 1 of 3 competitive losses
   - **Wrenholt Clinics** (D-1007 · \$45,000 · lost at Negotiation · we lost to Pindleworth): “We needed the HL7 feed on day one and that's on your roadmap, not in the product.” — Clinical ops lead · [Wrenholt Clinics loss debrief, Sep 30](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w11)
   - Deals: Wrenholt Clinics \(D-1007\)

### No-decision losses (2 deals)

_Every cited reason is a no-decision category in the taxonomy (for example they stayed with the status quo)._

1. **No decision\: stayed with the status quo** — 1 of 2 no-decision losses
   - **Plimsoll & Quist** (D-1003 · \$18,000 · lost at Evaluation): “Honestly we're going to stick with the spreadsheets this year and look again in spring.” — Operations director · [Plimsoll & Quist evaluation check-in, Jul 14](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w05)
   - **Plimsoll & Quist** (D-1003 · \$18,000 · lost at Evaluation): [CRM field “Closed lost reason”](https://crm.tamsquill.example/deals/D-1003): “No decision”
   - Deals: Plimsoll & Quist \(D-1003\)
2. **No decision\: timing or other priorities** — 1 of 2 no-decision losses
   - **Dovecrane Logistics** (D-1008 · \$15,000 · lost at Discovery): [CRM field “Closed lost reason”](https://crm.tamsquill.example/deals/D-1008): “Timing - revisit in Q1”
   - Deals: Dovecrane Logistics \(D-1008\)

### Other losses (1 deal)

_Lost with a cited reason, but not to a named competitor and not as no decision._

1. **Security, legal or compliance blocker** — 1 of 1 other loss
   - **Thrumcastle Supply** (D-1004 · \$32,000 · lost at Security review): “Without SAML single sign-on our IT team won't sign off, full stop.” — IT manager · [Thrumcastle Supply next steps, Aug 27](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w07)
   - Deals: Thrumcastle Supply \(D-1004\)

### Losses with no recorded reason (1 deal)

_No loss reason in the CRM fields read and none stated on the calls read. Not counted in any reason below; never read silence as a reason._

- **Corrabeck Studio** (D-1011 · lost at Evaluation) — 2 calls read

## Why we win

1. **Fast time to value** — 2 of 5 won deals (40%)
   - **Example Outfitters Co** (D-1001 · \$24,000): “We were live in a week, which is what sold the ops team.” — Head of Ops · [Example Outfitters trial review, Jul 28](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w01)
   - **Brimvasse Labs** (D-1012 · \$40,000): Note excerpt (AI meeting notes, not verbatim speech): _Two-week rollout plan was a deciding factor for the CTO._ · [Brimvasse Labs rollout planning, Sep 21](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w17)
   - **Example Outfitters Co** (D-1001 · \$24,000): [CRM field “Win reason”](https://crm.tamsquill.example/deals/D-1001): “Fast rollout”
   - Deals: Example Outfitters Co \(D-1001\); Brimvasse Labs \(D-1012\)
2. **Met security or compliance needs** — 1 of 5 won deals (20%)
   - **Brimvasse Labs** (D-1012 · \$40,000): “You were the only one with SAML and audit logs out of the box.” — CTO · [Brimvasse Labs security deep-dive, Sep 15](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w16)
   - Deals: Brimvasse Labs \(D-1012\)
3. **Solved the core use case** — 1 of 5 won deals (20%)
   - **Tarnwick Freight** (D-1009 · \$27,000): [CRM field “Win reason”](https://crm.tamsquill.example/deals/D-1009): “Product fit for multi-depot routing”
   - Deals: Tarnwick Freight \(D-1009\)
4. **Successful trial or proof of concept** — 1 of 5 won deals (20%)
   - **Example Outfitters Co** (D-1001 · \$24,000): Note excerpt (AI meeting notes, not verbatim speech): _Trial on two stores convinced the team; regional managers want the rest of the stores next._ · [Example Outfitters trial review, Jul 28](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w01)
   - Deals: Example Outfitters Co \(D-1001\)
5. **Integrations** — 1 of 5 won deals (20%)
   - **Quirnwell Studio** (D-1006 · \$12,000): “The fact that it talks to our project tool is the whole reason.” — Managing director · [Quirnwell Studio demo, Aug 25](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w09)
   - Deals: Quirnwell Studio \(D-1006\)
6. **Ease of use** — 1 of 5 won deals (20%)
   - **Brackenvolt Labs** (D-1005 · \$9,000): “My team just got it without training.” — Founder · [Brackenvolt Labs onboarding scope, Jul 2](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w08)
   - Deals: Brackenvolt Labs \(D-1005\)
7. **Price or value** — 1 of 5 won deals (20%)
   - **Brackenvolt Labs** (D-1005 · \$9,000): “And it fit the budget we had without a fight.” — Founder · [Brackenvolt Labs onboarding scope, Jul 2](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w08)
   - Deals: Brackenvolt Labs \(D-1005\)

## Competitor head-to-head

_Every figure is from our side: deals = deals where the CRM lists the competitor or we lost to them; "We won" = deals we won against them. Calls where a customer only mentioned them are counted separately and not rated._

| Competitor | Deals | We won | We lost to them | We lost otherwise | Our win rate | Mentioned on calls only |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Countwhistle | 5 | 3 | 2 | 0 | 60% | 0 |
| Pindleworth | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | n<5 | 0 |

- **Countwhistle** — 5 deals against them; we won 3 of 5 (60%); we lost to them: Marrowby & Vane \(D-1002\); Sallowfen Dental \(D-1010\)
   - **Example Outfitters Co** (D-1001): “Countwhistle came back with a lower number, but they wanted eight weeks to set up.” — Head of Ops · [Example Outfitters commercial close, Aug 12](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w02)

   - **Quirnwell Studio** (D-1006): “Countwhistle couldn't pull client data from our project tool at all.” — Managing director · [Quirnwell Studio demo, Aug 25](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w09)
- **Pindleworth** — 1 deal against them; we won 0 of 1; we lost to them: Wrenholt Clinics \(D-1007\)
   - **Wrenholt Clinics** (D-1007): “Pindleworth is already in the building, so you have to be clearly better, not just a bit better.” — Clinical ops lead · [Wrenholt Clinics negotiation, Sep 2](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w10)
   - **Wrenholt Clinics** (D-1007): “Pindleworth already runs our scheduling, so adding their module was the easy path.” — Clinical ops lead · [Wrenholt Clinics loss debrief, Sep 30](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w11)
- **Ostlemere** — mentioned on calls in 1 deal (not in the CRM's competitor field)
   - **Thrumcastle Supply** (D-1004): “We also looked at Ostlemere, but they have the same single sign-on gap.” — IT manager \(speaker unconfirmed\) · [Thrumcastle Supply security review, Jul 9](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w06)

## Objections raised before a loss

_From calls on or before each deal's close date. Recurring = raised in 2 or more lost deals._

- **Competitive comparison** — before the loss in 2 lost deals; also raised in 0 won deals

   - **Sallowfen Dental** (D-1010): Note excerpt (AI meeting notes, not verbatim speech): _Concerned about price compared with Countwhistle's quote._ · [Sallowfen Dental proposal walkthrough, Sep 1](https://notes.granola.ai/d/sample-w12)
